scope: Independent recomputation from 15 graph-eval-*.json files; no analyzer aggregate imported, no model or paid calls.

methods.summary: Arithmetic means and unbiased sample SD across three seeds. CE is mean negative log probability in nats per example. Accuracy is percent; differences are percentage points.
methods.paired_ci: Treatment minus residual-dense within each seed. Two-sided 95% Student-t CI: mean +/- 4.302652729911275 * sample_sd / sqrt(3), df=2. No multiple-comparison correction.
methods.time: Full 100-epoch synchronized training_seconds, separately total_run_seconds. Selected accumulated training time is an observed checkpoint time, not an early-stopped invocation or matched-quality runtime.

macs.interpretation: Realized skip counts weighted by nominal affine forward multiply-accumulates. Ignores bias, activation, crop/add, optimizer, data movement and kernel overhead; not profiler FLOPs or measured energy. Every full branch bypass also omits its affine backward computation; this calculation does not separately measure backward cost.

interpretation: At the validation-CE-selected primary endpoint, constant SD has lower test accuracy in every seed and its unadjusted paired 95% CI excludes zero; decreasing SD also has lower accuracy in every seed but its interval includes zero.

At fixed epoch100, both SD mean test accuracies are slightly above residual-dense, but both paired accuracy intervals include zero. Their final test CE is higher in every seed. Selection endpoint and evaluation metric materially alter the impression.

Validation-selected SD checkpoints have greater full-training CE and smaller train/test CE gaps, but this compares different selected epochs. A smaller gap by itself is not evidence of better held-out predictions.

At matched epoch10 the mean deterministic training-probe CE is 0.00084183 for residual-dense, 0.01017625 for constant SD, and 0.01532888 for decreasing SD. This supports delayed early fitting, but all three attain 100% full-training accuracy at epoch100; it does not establish improved generalization.

At epoch100 every SD model has approximately zero full-training CE and essentially perfect train accuracy. These data do not support a sustained inability to fit training data as the benefit of SD. The final deterministic dense training loss is distinct from stochastic training loss.

The direct execution result is robust: both SD arms reduce realized nominal affine MACs by about14.6% and full100-epoch training time by about14.3% versus the matched residual-dense control. This is a measured fixed-horizon speed result, not a matched-target-quality speedup.

Plain has higher mean final accuracy than either SD arm and has a different validation-selected LR. The added residual architecture is a substantive intervention; SD should primarily be compared with residual-dense.

Only3 seeds, one data split and one reused official test set; no multiple-comparison correction. The separate baseline optimization already inspected MNIST test outcomes, so the overall investigation is exploratory.
